 BASKETBALL Los Angeles Lakers Where to watch LA Lakers vs Golden State Warriors and what time is tonight's game?
 Lakers and Warriors light up Crypto.com Arena: Dončić versus Curry in a Western Conference classic
 Lakers vs Warriors Special 
 BEATRIZ RODRÍGUEZ
 Updated 21/10/2026
 -
 12:03 CDT 
 Follow MARCA on Google

 Los Angeles Lakers.  Lakers face backlash for moving on from Dalton Knecht despite his better numbers than Bronny James 
 Few matchups kick off a regular-season week with the shine this one has. The Los Angeles Lakers host the Golden State Warriors at the Crypto.com Arena, a showdown that brings together two franchises with winning DNA, two rosters packed with marquee names, and a rivalry that always raises the temperature in Southern California.
 Here we tell you everything: the schedule, where to watch it in the United States, and the keys that will decide the game.
 Lakers vs Warriors: Time and where to watch it
 The matchup is scheduled for the night of this Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 10:00 p.m. Eastern Time (9:00 p.m. Central Time and 7:00 p.m. Pacific Time). The venue will be the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angele s, an arena with a capacity of around 20,000 fans that promises a vibrant sellout for one of the most attractive visits on the schedule.
 In the United States, the broadcast is handled by the NBA’s television partners, but you can watch the Lakers vs. Warriors game live on ESPN. For those who follow the league outside the country and those who prefer to watch it via streaming, NBA League Pass offers the game online worldwide.
 How do the LA Lakers vs Golden State Warriors arrive for today's game?
 Both teams arrive without any games played in the season standings, so this matchup serves as a true statement of intent. The Lakers appear in 14th place in the overall standings and the Warriors in 10th, but those numbers are merely a starting point: what is at stake is the emotional tone for starting the campaign on the right foot in the always fierce Western Conference.
 The sportsbook clearly tips the scales toward the home team: the Lakers open as favorites with an implied probability of 66.3%, compared to the Warriors’ 33.7%. The total points line (over/under) sits around 234 points, a sign that the market anticipates a high-tempo game with plenty of scoring.
 In the point spread, the Lakers are carrying a line around -6 / -6.5, reflecting the advantage of playing at home and the depth of the Los Angeles roster.
 The Lakers' project revolves around Luka Dončić, the 27-year-old Slovenian who combines vision, ball-handling, and elite scoring ability. Alongside him, the backcourt has experience with Austin Reaves and the explosive Collin Sexton, while Quentin Grimes provides shooting and perimeter defense.
 In theory, the defensive-minded signing of Walker Kessler and the championship experience of Kevon Looney give Los Angeles presence in the paint and rim protection. The bench is rounded out with versatile pieces like Jake LaRavia, Jarred Vanderbilt, and Matisse Thybulle, a defensive specialist who can make life difficult for opposing shooters. Also on the roster is 22-year-old Bronny James, looking for minutes in the rotation.
 For their part, Golden State continues building around its legend: Stephen Curry, at 38 years old, remains the offensive focal point and the league's most feared trigger man from beyond the arc.
 The roster is loaded with veteran experience and talent: 37-year-old Jimmy Butler brings toughness, scoring in key moments, and leadership; Draymond Green remains the defensive brain and the glue of the team; and Latvian Kristaps Porziņģis adds height, blocks, and an outside shooting threat from the center position.
 The roster is rounded out by the experienced 40-year-old Al Horford, along with rising youngsters like Brandin Podziemski and Moses Moody, with Georges Niang and Gary Payton II strengthening the rotation.
 What is the forecast for the game between the Lakers vs Warriors?
 With the advantage of playing at home, the status of favorites set by the market, and a roster balanced between offensive talent and defensive solidity, the Lakers have the arguments to prevail.
 That said, the Warriors' experience and firepower—with Curry capable of turning a score around in minutes—guarantee that it will not be a walk in the park. The outlook points to a high-scoring game, in line with the total near 234 points: a narrow Lakers victory, in an outcome that could very well be decided in the final quarter.
